chapters.1.summary: The book opens with a list of names and no story. It runs from Adam through Noah to Noah’s three sons. It names the peoples that came from Japheth, Ham, and Shem. Shem’s line leads to Abraham. Abraham’s sons are Isaac and Ishmael, with more sons by Keturah. Isaac’s sons are Esau and Israel. The rest of the chapter lists Esau’s family and the kings and chiefs of Edom.
chapters.1.lds: Why might the book begin with Adam instead of David?
chapters.2.summary: The chapter lists the twelve sons of Israel and then follows Judah. Judah’s first sons were born to a Canaanite woman. Tamar, his daughter-in-law, bore him Perez and Zerah. The line of Perez runs through Boaz and Jesse to David, the seventh son. David’s sisters and their warrior sons are named. Long lists follow for Caleb’s and Jerahmeel’s families. One man with no sons gives his daughter to his Egyptian servant. The chapter ends with families of scribes who were Kenites.
chapters.2.lds: Which women and people from other lands appear in Judah’s family?
chapters.3.summary: The chapter lists David’s sons born in Hebron and in Jerusalem. It names his daughter Tamar. Then it lists the kings of Judah from Solomon to Josiah’s sons. Jeconiah, also called Jehoiachin, is named “the captive.” His sons include Shealtiel and Pedaiah. Zerubbabel appears in the next generation. The list continues for several generations after the exile.
chapters.3.lds: What hope might a surviving royal family give people after exile?
chapters.4.summary: The chapter adds more clans of Judah. A man named Jabez prays for blessing, more land, and protection from harm. God grants his request. The list names a valley of craftsmen, a guild of linen workers, and royal potters. Then it turns to Simeon’s towns in the south. Some Simeonites move to find pasture for their flocks. In Hezekiah’s time they take land at Gedor. Others defeat a remnant of Amalek at Mount Seir.
chapters.4.lds: What does Jabez ask God to protect him from?
chapters.5.summary: Reuben was Israel’s firstborn, but he lost the birthright by wronging his father. It passed to Joseph’s sons, while Judah produced the ruler. The chapter lists Reuben, Gad, and the half tribe of Manasseh east of the Jordan. In a war with the Hagrites they cry to God, and he helps them. They take many animals and captives. Later these tribes are unfaithful and follow the gods of the land. God stirs up the king of Assyria, who carries them away.
chapters.5.lds: The Seminary manual connects these passages with trust and repentance. Why did Reuben lose the birthright (verse 1)?
chapters.6.summary: This chapter lists the families of Levi. It traces the high priests from Aaron to the exile. It gives the families of Gershom, Kohath, and Merari. The prophet Samuel appears in the line of Kohath. David appointed Heman, Asaph, and Ethan to lead the singing. Other Levites did the remaining work of the tabernacle. Aaron’s sons alone served at the altars. The chapter ends with the towns given to the Levites in every tribe.
chapters.6.lds: How do the singers’ duties differ from the priests’ duties?
chapters.7.summary: The chapter lists families of Issachar, Benjamin, Naphtali, Manasseh, Ephraim, and Asher. It counts their fighting men. In Ephraim’s family, men of Gath kill sons who came to take cattle. Ephraim mourns many days, and his brothers come to comfort him. He names his next son Beriah because of the trouble. His daughter Sheerah builds three towns. Joshua son of Nun comes from this line.
chapters.7.lds: Which work by women does this family list remember?
chapters.8.summary: The chapter gives a long list of Benjamin’s families. Some heads of families lived in Jerusalem. Others lived at Gibeon. The list reaches Ner, Kish, and Saul. Saul’s sons include Jonathan and Eshbaal. Jonathan’s line continues through Merib-baal and Micah for many generations. The last family named has sons who were skilled archers.
chapters.8.lds: How does Saul’s family list prepare for the next part of the book?
chapters.9.summary: All Israel was listed, and Judah was exiled for unfaithfulness. The chapter names the first people who lived again in Jerusalem. They come from Judah, Benjamin, Ephraim, and Manasseh. Priests, Levites, and temple servants are counted. Gatekeepers guard the four sides of God’s house. Some Levites count the vessels, and others care for flour, wine, oil, and spices. One bakes the flat bread, and singers serve day and night. Saul’s family list is repeated at the end.
chapters.9.lds: What daily tasks keep the temple’s worship working?
chapters.10.summary: The Philistines defeat Israel on Mount Gilboa. Saul’s three sons are killed, and archers wound him. He falls on his own sword. The Philistines strip him and put his head in the temple of Dagon. Men of Jabesh Gilead take the bodies and bury them. The writer says Saul died for his unfaithfulness. He did not keep the LORD’s word, and he consulted a medium. So the LORD gave the kingdom to David.
chapters.10.lds: The Seminary manual uses Saul’s final notice to discuss trust and obedience. What three failures do verses 13–14 name?
chapters.11.summary: All Israel comes to Hebron and anoints David king. He captures Jebus, which is Jerusalem. Joab goes up first and becomes commander. The chapter then lists David’s mighty men. One stood his ground in a barley field against the Philistines. Three broke through enemy lines to bring David water from Bethlehem. Abishai and Benaiah are praised for their deeds. A long list of warriors follows, and it includes Uriah the Hittite.
chapters.11.lds: Why does David refuse water that his men risk their lives to bring?
chapters.12.summary: Fighting men join David while he hides from Saul at Ziklag. Some are from Benjamin, Saul’s own tribe. Men of Gad cross the Jordan in flood to reach him. The Spirit moves Amasai to pledge loyalty and peace to David. More men desert to him from Manasseh. At Hebron every tribe sends armed men to make him king. They feast with David for three days. Neighbors from far in the north bring food on donkeys, camels, mules, and oxen.
chapters.12.lds: How do David’s supporters help beyond bringing weapons?
chapters.13.summary: David consults his commanders and the whole assembly about the ark. All agree to bring it from Kiriath Jearim. They carry it on a new cart with music and singing. At a threshing floor the oxen stumble. Uzza puts out his hand to steady the ark, and God strikes him dead. David is angry and then afraid. He leaves the ark at the house of Obed-Edom. The LORD blesses that household for three months.
chapters.13.lds: Why does David stop moving the ark? What changes when he tries again?
chapters.14.summary: King Hiram of Tyre sends cedar and builders for David’s house. David sees that the LORD has established him for Israel’s sake. He takes more wives and has more children in Jerusalem. The Philistines raid the Valley of Rephaim. David asks God, attacks, and wins. The Philistines raid the same valley again. David asks again and is told to circle behind them. He waits for the sound of marching in the trees and wins.
chapters.14.lds: Why does David ask for guidance before each battle?
chapters.15.summary: David prepares a tent for the ark in Jerusalem. He says only Levites may carry it. He gathers the priests and Levites and tells them to make themselves holy. They carry the ark on poles on their shoulders, as Moses commanded. David appoints singers and players of cymbals, harps, and lyres. God helps the Levites, and they offer sacrifices. All Israel brings up the ark with shouting and trumpets. Michal sees David dancing and despises him.
chapters.15.lds: What changes when David tries again to move the ark?
chapters.16.summary: The ark is set in its tent, and David offers sacrifices. He gives every person bread, meat, and raisins. He appoints Levites to thank and praise the LORD before the ark. Asaph and his brothers sing a psalm of thanks. It calls the nations to praise and recalls the covenant with Abraham. The people answer, “Amen.” David leaves Asaph to serve before the ark every day. Zadok and the priests offer the daily sacrifices at the tabernacle in Gibeon.
chapters.16.lds: The Seminary manual connects this song with continuing gratitude and praise. What work does David assign after the celebration (verse 37)?
chapters.17.summary: David tells Nathan that he lives in cedar while the ark sits in a tent. Nathan tells him to do what is in his heart. That night God gives Nathan a different message. David will not build the house. God took him from the sheep and will build him a house instead. A son will build the temple, and his throne will last forever. David sits before the LORD and asks who he is to receive this. He prays that God will do as he has said.
chapters.17.lds: How does God’s promise change David’s plan for a temple?
chapters.18.summary: David defeats the Philistines and takes Gath. He defeats Moab, and the Moabites bring tribute. He defeats Hadadezer of Zobah and the Syrians who come to help. He takes gold shields and a great amount of bronze. Solomon later uses that bronze for the temple. King Tou of Hamath sends gifts. David dedicates all the silver and gold to the LORD. Abishai defeats Edom, and the chapter lists David’s officers.
chapters.18.lds: Where does David place the treasure gained from war?
chapters.19.summary: The king of Ammon dies, and David sends men to comfort his son Hanun. Hanun’s princes say the men have come to spy. Hanun shaves them and cuts off their clothes at the hips. David tells the shamed men to wait at Jericho. Ammon hires chariots and horsemen from Syria for a thousand talents of silver. Joab and Abishai fight on two fronts and win. The Syrians bring more troops from beyond the River. David defeats them, and they make peace.
chapters.19.lds: Come, Follow Me specifically compares this story with 2 Samuel 10–12. What do Hanun’s princes claim in verse 3?
chapters.20.summary: In spring Joab leads the army against Ammon and besieges Rabbah. David stays in Jerusalem. Joab takes the city. David takes the heavy gold crown of its king and much plunder. He puts the people to work with saws, picks, and axes. Later wars with the Philistines follow. David’s men kill three giants, one of them Goliath’s brother. One giant has six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot.
chapters.20.lds: Come, Follow Me notes that Chronicles omits negative stories about David. Compare verse 1 with 2 Samuel 11:1. What story does Chronicles leave out?
chapters.21.summary: Satan moves David to count Israel. Joab objects but obeys, and he leaves out Levi and Benjamin. God is displeased and strikes Israel. The prophet Gad offers David three punishments. David chooses to fall into the LORD’s hand. A plague kills seventy thousand. David sees the angel standing over Jerusalem with a drawn sword. He buys Ornan’s threshing floor, builds an altar, and fire from heaven answers him.
chapters.21.lds: David asks why the people must suffer. What does his response show about responsibility?
chapters.22.summary: David says the threshing floor is the place for God’s house. He gathers stonecutters and stores up iron, bronze, and cedar. Solomon is young, so David prepares in great quantity. He tells Solomon that he wanted to build the house himself. The LORD refused because David had shed much blood. A son named Solomon, a man of rest, would build it. David hands over gold, silver, and workers. He orders Israel’s leaders to help his son.
chapters.22.lds: How does David help a task that someone else will finish?
chapters.23.summary: David is old and makes Solomon king. He counts the Levites aged thirty and above. There are thirty-eight thousand. Most will oversee the work of the LORD’s house. Others will be officers, judges, gatekeepers, and musicians. The families of Gershon, Kohath, and Merari are listed. The Levites will no longer carry the tabernacle. They will help the priests with courts, rooms, bread, flour, measures, and daily praise.
chapters.23.lds: Which temple duties involve ordinary food, measures, and supplies?
chapters.24.summary: David organizes the priests, the sons of Aaron. Eleazar’s family has sixteen heads, and Ithamar’s has eight. They are divided by lot, since both families have leaders. A Levite scribe records the result before the king and the priests. Twenty-four divisions are named in order. The eighth lot falls to Abijah. The remaining Levites also cast lots for their duties. The chief’s household and the youngest brother’s are treated alike.
chapters.24.lds: How does drawing lots share duties among priestly families?
chapters.25.summary: David and his commanders set apart musicians for the temple. They come from the families of Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun. They are to prophesy with lyres, harps, and cymbals. Heman has fourteen sons and three daughters. All serve under their fathers’ direction. There are two hundred eighty-eight trained singers. They cast lots for their duties. Twenty-four groups of twelve are listed in order.
chapters.25.lds: Why does the music list include both teachers and students?
chapters.26.summary: The chapter lists the gatekeepers by family. Obed-Edom has sixty-two able descendants, for God blessed him. One father makes a younger son chief. Lots decide which family guards each gate. Guards are posted daily on every side. Other Levites keep the treasuries and the dedicated gifts. These gifts include spoil given by Samuel, Saul, Abner, and Joab. Still others serve as officers and judges across Israel.
chapters.26.lds: What does faithful care of temple supplies require?
chapters.27.summary: The chapter lists the army’s twelve divisions. Each has twenty-four thousand men and serves one month a year. A leader is named for each tribe. David did not count those under twenty, since God promised many descendants. Stewards manage the king’s storehouses, fields, vineyards, and olive trees. Others manage herds, camels, donkeys, and flocks. Two of these stewards are foreigners. The king’s counselors are named last.
chapters.27.lds: Which workers support the kingdom through farming and storage?
chapters.28.summary: David gathers Israel’s leaders in Jerusalem and stands to speak. He wanted to build a house for the ark. God refused him as a man of war and chose Solomon. David charges Solomon to know God and serve him with a whole heart. He gives him the plans for every room and court. He gives the weights of gold and silver for each lampstand, table, and bowl. He says all of it came in writing from the LORD’s hand. He tells Solomon to be strong and do the work.
chapters.28.lds: The Seminary manual emphasizes seeking God and courage in service. What does David tell Solomon to do in verse 20?
chapters.29.summary: David tells the assembly what he has given for the temple from his own treasure. The leaders give gold, silver, bronze, iron, and precious stones. The people rejoice because the gifts are given freely. David blesses the LORD before them all. He says everything in heaven and earth belongs to God. He asks God to keep the people’s hearts loyal and to help Solomon. Solomon is made king, and Zadok priest. David dies at a good old age, full of days, riches, and honor.
chapters.29.lds: The Seminary manual studies named records and revelation beyond the Bible. What do these records tell readers about David’s rule?
